learningObjective: Reason about the split between one-time build cost and per-inference runtime cost in TensorRT, and identify a common misdiagnosis when comparing to eager PyTorch.

canonicalClaims.claim: TensorRT builder cost is a one-time offline expense (tactic search, calibration, memory planning); per-inference latency of the deserialized engine is the meaningful deployment metric. Conflating the two produces misleading comparisons.
conditions: Standard TensorRT build → serialize → deploy workflow.
Benchmark aims to reflect steady-state serving cost.
nonImplications: Does not imply build time is unimportant; it matters for development velocity and rebuild-on-config-change.
Does not imply TRT is always faster at inference.

misconceptions.claim: TRT rebuilds on every inference call.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Build is one-time; runtime deserializes the plan.

misconceptions.claim: TRT is always slower than PyTorch eager.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TRT frequently outperforms eager, particularly on transformers with fusion and INT8/FP8.

misconceptions.claim: Build time and inference time should be added.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They belong in different columns: build is offline amortized cost; inference is per-request.

misconceptions.claim: Eager PyTorch requires no synchronization to measure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Eager PyTorch is asynchronous with respect to CUDA and requires synchronize for correct timing.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA best practices; PyTorch profiler docs
